sentences.en: So, Kash, you've covered so many different types of surveillance at this point.
sentences.zh: 那么，卡什，到目前为止你已经报道过各种类型的监控了。

sentences.en: I know a lot of Americans are aware that they are being watched in sort of one form or another, whether it's online or in public spaces.
sentences.zh: 我知道很多美国人都意识到他们正以某种形式被监视，无论是在网上还是在公共场所。

sentences.en: So, can you just start off by explaining what is so different about this particular kind of surveillance and why it's prompted people to finally say, like, enough is enough?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能先解释一下这种特殊的监控有什么不同，以及为什么它最终促使人们说“受够了”吗？

sentences.en: So, these are cameras that take photos of cars and read their license plates.
sentences.zh: 这些摄像头会拍摄汽车照片并读取车牌。

sentences.en: If you start looking around as you're driving, you might see them on a pole, by the road, solar panel, camera looking down your way.
sentences.zh: 如果你开车时四处看看，可能会在路边的杆子上看到它们，有太阳能板，摄像头正对着你的方向。

sentences.en: And they're in places where people maybe aren't used to being surveilled.
sentences.zh: 它们出现在人们可能不习惯被监控的地方。

sentences.en: You know, they're in rural roads, just in communities that don't necessarily have a lot of other cameras around.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们出现在乡村道路上，出现在那些周围并没有太多其他摄像头的社区里。

sentences.en: Also, people do have this kind of privacy attachment to their cars.
sentences.zh: 此外，人们对自己的汽车有一种隐私依恋。

sentences.en: And so, I think Americans kind of think of your car as this kind of symbol of freedom,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为美国人把汽车视为一种自由的象征，

sentences.en: this thing you can get away from everyone, but now you can't because there are going to be cameras tracking it.
sentences.zh: 一种可以让你远离所有人的东西，但现在你做不到了，因为会有摄像头追踪它。

sentences.en: And so, my colleague Fernando Alfonso and I found that people were just getting really upset about these cameras.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的同事费尔南多·阿方索和我发现人们对这些摄像头感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: And it was a level of uproar over privacy that I haven't seen before, or at least haven't seen in a very long time.
sentences.zh: 这种对隐私的抗议程度是我以前从未见过的，或者至少是很久没见过的。

sentences.en: So, what is the camera capturing exactly?

sentences.en: Just the license plate?

sentences.en: Or is it something more complicated than that?
sentences.zh: 还是比那更复杂？

sentences.en: Because on its face, a license plate reader, that sort of sounds a bit benign.
sentences.zh: 因为从表面上看，车牌识别器听起来似乎没什么害处。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, the cameras take photos of cars as they pass.
sentences.zh: 摄像头会在汽车经过时拍摄照片。

sentences.en: They get the license plate, but you can also use a system to search other things,
sentences.zh: 它们获取车牌信息，但你也可以使用系统搜索其他东西，

sentences.en: like the color of the car, the make of the car, whether it has a bumper sticker or visible damage or a toolbox on the back.
sentences.zh: 比如汽车颜色、品牌，是否有保险杠贴纸、明显的损坏或后部的工具箱。

sentences.en: And this gives police more visibility into our movements than they've ever had before.
sentences.zh: 这让警方对我们行踪的掌控力达到了前所未有的程度。

sentences.en: So, Flock was founded by a serial entrepreneur named Garrett Langley.
sentences.zh: Flock是由一位连续创业者加勒特·兰利创立的。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.

sentences.en: I'm Kashmir.

sentences.en: I actually met with him a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 我几周前确实见过他。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you, Kashmir.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你，克什米尔。

sentences.en: You're in New York, right?
sentences.zh: 你在纽约，对吧？

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He said he got the idea because he lived in Atlanta, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 他说他有这个想法是因为他住在佐治亚州的亚特兰大。

sentences.en: That's where the company is headquartered.
sentences.zh: 那是公司总部所在地。

sentences.en: I started the company nine years ago, knowing nothing about law enforcement, public safety,
sentences.zh: 我九年前创办了这家公司，当时对执法和公共安全一无所知，

sentences.en: just this, like, confusion as an engineer of why it was so easy to get away with crime in America.
sentences.zh: 只是作为一个工程师，对为什么在美国犯罪这么容易逃脱感到困惑。

sentences.en: And in his neighborhood, people kept breaking into cars on the weekends.
sentences.zh: 在他的社区里，人们周末总是破窗入车行窃。

sentences.en: And we kept having the same group, seemingly the same group, come in on a Friday night.
sentences.zh: 我们总是遇到同一伙人，看起来是同一伙人，在周五晚上过来。

sentences.en: And he said taking guns out of the glove boxes.
sentences.zh: 他说他们从手套箱里拿走枪支。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It was happening every weekend.
sentences.zh: 这每个周末都在发生。

sentences.en: He was really frustrated.
sentences.zh: 他真的很沮丧。

sentences.en: And so when I was talking to our zone commander, I was like,
sentences.zh: 所以当我和我们的区域指挥官交谈时，我说，

sentences.en: Major, why can't you catch these people?
sentences.zh: 少校，你为什么抓不到这些人？

sentences.en: Like, do something about this.
sentences.zh: 做点什么吧。

sentences.en: And so we called the police department.
sentences.zh: 于是我们给警察局打了电话。

sentences.en: And he was like, what do you expect me to do?
sentences.zh: 他说，你指望我做什么？

sentences.en: We're not the CSI on TV.
sentences.zh: 我们又不是电视里的CSI。

sentences.en: I'm not going to, like, I'm one guy.
sentences.zh: 我没法……我只是一个人。

sentences.en: And I was like, well, but they're stealing guns.
sentences.zh: 我说，但是他们在偷枪啊。

sentences.en: Like, this is crazy.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And he said that the person he talked to said that they needed their license plate numbers.
sentences.zh: 他说他交谈的那个人说他们需要车牌号。

sentences.en: I was like, what?
sentences.zh: 我说，什么？

sentences.en: What are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 你在说什么？

sentences.en: What would a license plate do in this situation?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下车牌能起什么作用？

sentences.en: How would it help?
sentences.zh: 它怎么会有帮助？

sentences.en: He was like, trust me, a license plate is the most actionable piece of evidence we can get.
sentences.zh: 他说，相信我，车牌是我们能得到的最具可操作性的证据。

sentences.en: And I said, fine.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧。

sentences.en: And I called a page of Matt and I was like, here's what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 我给马特打了电话，我说，我们要这样做。

sentences.en: We're going to build license plate reading cameras for neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 我们要为社区制造车牌识别摄像头。

sentences.en: So he decided to create this product along with two of his classmates from Georgia Tech.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定和他在佐治亚理工学院的两位同学一起开发这个产品。

sentences.en: This is literally like we were just messing around conceptually.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像我们当时只是在概念上瞎搞。

sentences.en: They wanted to make cheap license plate readers, basically put a phone together with a solar panel.
sentences.zh: 他们想制造廉价的车牌识别器，基本上就是把手机和太阳能板组合在一起。

sentences.en: It hooked up to an old Android with a solar power.
sentences.zh: 它连接到一个旧的安卓手机和太阳能电源上。

sentences.en: That you could put on street poles and it would just get photos of cars that were driving paSt.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它装在路灯杆上，它就能拍下经过的汽车照片。

sentences.en: And so we built a bunch.
sentences.zh: 于是我们造了一堆。

sentences.en: We put them up in a couple neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 我们把它们装在几个社区里。

sentences.en: And for the first probably two or three years, we were only selling to neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 头两三年，我们只卖给社区。

sentences.en: Flock first started selling these to homeowners associations, kind of like an automated neighborhood watch.
sentences.zh: Flock最初是把这些卖给业主协会，有点像自动化的社区巡逻。

sentences.en: So you could, you know, see who was coming and going.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以知道谁来了又走了。

sentences.en: If there was a package theft, you could see, well, what car was there and drove away.
sentences.zh: 如果发生了包裹失窃，你可以看到是哪辆车停在那儿然后开走了。

sentences.en: And like two months into the business, we made our first arreSt.
sentences.zh: 业务开展大概两个月后，我们就完成了第一次逮捕。

sentences.en: And just a few months after they start installing these devices, Langley said that he got a call from the police telling him that it was helping to solve crime.
sentences.zh: 在开始安装这些设备仅几个月后，兰利说他接到了警方的电话，告诉他这有助于破案。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh my gosh, like it works.
sentences.zh: 我说，天哪，它真的管用。

sentences.en: This major wasn't lying to me.
sentences.zh: 那位少校没骗我。

sentences.en: They actually just need evidence.
sentences.zh: 他们确实只需要证据。

sentences.en: If they have evidence, they will prosecute a case.
sentences.zh: 如果他们有证据，他们就会起诉案件。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: OK, so in this moment, this is like basically his proof of concept.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以在那一刻，这基本上就是他的概念验证。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: How do things go from there?
sentences.zh: 从那以后情况如何发展？

sentences.en: How does the company grow from there?
sentences.zh: 公司从那时起是如何成长的？

sentences.en: So in 2020, the company starts working for the first time with a police department in Jersey Village, Texas.
sentences.zh: 2020年，公司首次开始与得克萨斯州泽西村的警察局合作。

sentences.en: And this kind of changes the business model.
sentences.zh: 这改变了商业模式。

sentences.en: Instead of putting it on private streets, you're starting to put it on public roads.
sentences.zh: 不再是安装在私人街道上，而是开始安装在公共道路上。

sentences.en: And the business really exploded from there.
sentences.zh: 业务从那时起真正爆发了。

sentences.en: And they see a ton of success.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: And so that police chief is telling his friends, that mayor is telling her friends.
sentences.zh: 于是那位警察局长告诉他的朋友，那位市长告诉她的朋友。

sentences.en: They started working with police departments around the country.
sentences.zh: 他们开始与全国各地的警察局合作。

sentences.en: You need to get this in your town.
sentences.zh: 你需要把这个装在你的镇上。

sentences.en: Like, we're safer now.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我们现在更安全了。

sentences.en: And that word of mouth, you know, spread quite quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且那种口碑，你知道，传播得非常快。

sentences.en: And with that expansion has come a kind of growing backlash as communities are discovering that these cameras are there and how they're being used.
sentences.zh: 随着这种扩张，也出现了一种日益增长的抵制情绪，因为社区开始发现这些摄像头就在那里，以及它们是如何被使用的。

sentences.en: I want to talk about the backlash.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈这种抵制情绪。

sentences.en: But before we do, I just want to understand what the police departments are actually using these cameras for and how they are being used.
sentences.zh: 但在我们开始之前，我只是想了解警察部门到底用这些摄像头做什么，以及它们是如何被使用的。

sentences.en: So can you just describe a little bit the mechanics of this?
sentences.zh: 所以，你能简单描述一下这背后的运作机制吗？

sentences.en: So what these cameras allow police departments to do is essentially to track cars.
sentences.zh: 这些摄像头让警察部门能够做的事情，本质上就是追踪车辆。

sentences.en: Most of the departments keep the photos of the cars for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 大多数部门会将车辆照片保存30天。

sentences.en: That's the default that Flock has in place.
sentences.zh: 这是Flock设定的默认期限。

sentences.en: And so if somebody goes missing or if there is some kind of crime that is committed and you know the car associated with the crime, you can go looking for it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有人失踪，或者发生了某种犯罪，而你知道与犯罪相关的车辆，你就可以去寻找它。

sentences.en: You can see where it's been.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它去过哪里。

sentences.en: You can see where it's gone.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它去了哪里。

sentences.en: You can also set up alerts.
sentences.zh: 你还可以设置警报。

sentences.en: So if there is a car you're looking for, it'll shoot up an alert to any police that are using this network, whether it's in your community or in a different community.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你正在寻找某辆车，它会向所有使用该网络的警察发送警报，无论是在你的社区还是在其他社区。

sentences.en: Basically, any crime that's committed using a car, this system might be helpful with, which is a lot of crimes.
sentences.zh: 基本上，任何使用车辆进行的犯罪，这个系统都可能有所帮助，而这涵盖了大量的犯罪。

sentences.en: A lot of crimes use cars.
sentences.zh: 很多犯罪都会用到车辆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's helpful for tracking down stolen cars, finding a missing person.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它对于追踪被盗车辆、寻找失踪人员很有帮助。

sentences.en: I mean, we've all gotten those Amber Alerts on our text messages where it says, you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们都收到过那种安珀警报（Amber Alerts）的短信，上面写着，你知道的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I was just thinking of that.
sentences.zh: 我刚才就在想这个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like, look around for this random Nissan Altima with this license plate.
sentences.zh: 就像是，留意一下这辆挂着这个车牌的普通日产Altima。

sentences.en: It's a lot more effective just to send that message out through a bunch of cameras that have their eyes on the road to find that car.
sentences.zh: 通过一堆盯着道路的摄像头来发送那条消息，以找到那辆车，要有效得多。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So by this point in the story, these cameras are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以故事讲到这里，这些摄像头已经随处可见了。

sentences.en: The company's grown super faSt.
sentences.zh: 这家公司发展得超级快。

sentences.en: I just want to make sure I understand the legality of this.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确保我理解这其中的合法性。

sentences.en: Does Flock need anybody's permission to put these cameras up on streets or do they just put these things up and then sell the data?
sentences.zh: Flock在街道上安装这些摄像头需要获得任何人的许可吗？还是他们直接把这些东西装上，然后就开始售卖数据？

sentences.en: This is actually an issue for the company.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是该公司面临的一个问题。

sentences.en: And I talked about that with the CEO.
sentences.zh: 我和首席执行官谈过这件事。

sentences.en: You know, in the early days when they were working with neighborhood associations, it was private streets.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在他们与社区协会合作的早期，那是私人街道。

sentences.en: They could just put them up.
sentences.zh: 他们可以直接安装。

sentences.en: As they started working with police, they still had this kind of move fast and break thing, Silicon Valley approach, where they would just go out and throw these cheap cameras up.
sentences.zh: 当他们开始与警方合作时，他们仍然采取那种“快速行动，打破常规”的硅谷式做法，直接出去把这些廉价的摄像头装上。

sentences.en: And that got them in trouble with departments of transportation where you are supposed to get a permit to be, you know, putting cameras in poles up on public roads.
sentences.zh: 这让他们在交通部门那里惹了麻烦，因为在公共道路的电线杆上安装摄像头是需要获得许可的。

sentences.en: And so Langley told me, yes, they made some mistakes, but now they have figured out the right way to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以Langley告诉我，是的，他们犯了一些错误，但现在他们已经找到了正确的方法。

sentences.en: It's so interesting to think about how fast this company has grown when this is effectively just like a camera on a stick.
sentences.zh: 想到这家公司成长得如此之快，而这实际上只是一个杆子上的摄像头，真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: Yes, it is just a camera on a stick.
sentences.zh: 是的，它确实只是一个杆子上的摄像头。

sentences.en: But now it's 120,000 cameras on sticks and they're all connected.
sentences.zh: 但现在它是12万个杆子上的摄像头，而且它们全都连接在一起。

sentences.en: And that is really what makes Flock so valuable.
sentences.zh: 而这正是Flock如此有价值的原因。

sentences.en: It's that they're building this network.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们正在构建的网络。

sentences.en: It's eyes on the road across the whole country.
sentences.zh: 这是遍布全国的道路之眼。

sentences.en: And that's something we really haven't had before at this scale.
sentences.zh: 这是我们以前从未达到过这种规模的东西。

sentences.en: And that's why police want to work with this company.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么警察想与这家公司合作的原因。

sentences.en: Okay, so this isn't just about necessarily your local police department being able to track your car.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这不一定只是关于你当地的警察部门能够追踪你的车辆。

sentences.en: This is about one camera.
sentences.zh: 这是关于一个摄像头。

sentences.en: I don't know what talking to another camera.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它在和另一个摄像头交流什么。

sentences.en: Like, just talk about that network for a second so we can understand why that makes this different than just something that might only affect an isolated area.
sentences.zh: 就像，简单谈谈那个网络，这样我们就能理解为什么这与仅仅影响孤立区域的东西不同。

sentences.en: So local police departments, when they sign up for Flock, essentially set their privacy settings.
sentences.zh: 所以当地警察部门在注册Flock时，基本上会设置他们的隐私设置。

sentences.en: They can decide if they want their network of cameras to only be available to their department or if they want to be able to make it available to the whole state or the whole nation.
sentences.zh: 他们可以决定是希望自己的摄像头网络仅供本部门使用，还是希望将其提供给整个州或整个国家使用。

sentences.en: And it's reciprocal.
sentences.zh: 而且这是互惠的。

sentences.en: If you want to be able to search all the cameras in your state or all the cameras in the whole country, you have to grant access to your cameras.
sentences.zh: 如果你想搜索你所在州或全国所有的摄像头，你就必须授予别人访问你摄像头的权限。

sentences.en: I asked Linley about this and he said the vast majority of their customers opt in for the national network.
sentences.zh: 我问过Linley这个问题，他说绝大多数客户都选择了加入全国网络。

sentences.en: Like, that is what's appealing, that you have eyes on the road everywhere, not just in your community, but in your whole state, in your whole country.
sentences.zh: 就像，这就是吸引力所在，你在任何地方都有道路之眼，不仅是在你的社区，而且是在你的整个州，你的整个国家。

sentences.en: Because, as they put it, you know, crime doesn't respect borders.
sentences.zh: 因为正如他们所说，你知道，犯罪是不分国界的。

sentences.en: And Flock gave me an example of why this is useful.
sentences.zh: Flock给了我一个例子来说明为什么这很有用。

sentences.en: In one case, there was somebody who had made a threat against an event in New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 有一次，有人对新奥尔良的一场活动发出了威胁。

sentences.en: And for some reason, police had a car associated with this threat.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，警方掌握了一辆与此威胁相关的车辆。

sentences.en: And the person was based in North Carolina, but when they picked him up, he was in Florida.
sentences.zh: 那个人住在北卡罗来纳州，但当他们抓到他时，他人在佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: And so this involves, you know, three different communities, three different states.
sentences.zh: 所以这涉及到了，你知道，三个不同的社区，三个不同的州。

sentences.en: And the only way they said, you know, you can really solve this crime is with these cameras that are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们说，解决这起犯罪的唯一方法就是使用这些随处可见的摄像头。

sentences.en: So basically, a big difference, it sounds like what you're saying, is that pre-Flock or without Flock,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，听起来你所说的一个巨大区别是，在Flock之前或没有Flock的情况下，

sentences.en: some police chief in one district might have to figure out who to call in another district, ask them to run a report.
sentences.zh: 某个地区的警察局长可能必须弄清楚该给另一个地区的谁打电话，请求他们运行一份报告。

sentences.en: And presumably, that takes longer than going to a database on your computer and typing in a license plate, in this case, right?
sentences.zh: 而且据推测，这比在电脑上打开数据库并输入车牌号要花更长时间，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is really faSt.
sentences.zh: 而且这真的很快。

sentences.en: They said, you know, it basically comes off their cameras, and within seconds, it's in the database.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你知道，它基本上从摄像头传出，几秒钟内就进入了数据库。

sentences.en: And it really is a pretty simple tool.
sentences.zh: 而且它确实是一个非常简单的工具。

sentences.en: You know, there is a search page where you are supposed to enter the case number, the crime that you're looking into.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一个搜索页面，你需要输入案件编号，也就是你正在调查的犯罪案件。

sentences.en: And then you can either put in the license plate number, or you can put in a description of the car, you know, the color, or if it has damage or bumper sticker.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以输入车牌号，或者输入车辆的描述，你知道，颜色，或者是否有损坏或保险杠贴纸。

sentences.en: Then you hit search, and it will pop up a grid of photos of the backs of people's cars.
sentences.zh: 然后点击搜索，它会弹出一个人们车尾照片的网格。

sentences.en: It will say where the photo was taken, when, and which agency's cameras took it.
sentences.zh: 它会显示照片拍摄的地点、时间，以及是哪个机构的摄像头拍摄的。

sentences.en: But it's pretty simple, but police say it makes their jobs much easier.
sentences.zh: 虽然很简单，但警察说这让他们的工作轻松多了。

sentences.en: The CEO of Flock says that the company helped solve more than a million crimes last year.
sentences.zh: Flock的首席执行官表示，该公司去年帮助解决了超过一百万起犯罪。

sentences.en: I don't have the reporting to back that up, but police chiefs did tell us that it is really a useful tool for solving crimes.
sentences.zh: 我没有相关报道来支持这一点，但警察局长们确实告诉我们，这确实是一个解决犯罪的有用工具。

sentences.en: But this makes it really easy to track Americans.
sentences.zh: 但这确实让追踪美国人变得非常容易。

sentences.en: And, you know, we're all in the database if you're driving cars in the 49 states where they have their cameras, and it's not just people who have committed crimes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你在他们拥有摄像头的49个州开车，我们都在数据库里，而且不仅仅是那些犯过罪的人。

sentences.en: And that is just making people very, very uncomfortable that this is too powerful a tool that is surveilling too many of us.
sentences.zh: 这让人们感到非常非常不安，因为这是一个太强大的工具，正在监视我们太多人。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是Winnalou。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉（promesthesia）的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Okay, so Kashmir, I understand from what you're saying that people are upset about these cameras and have a lot of different privacy concerns.
sentences.zh: 好的，Kashmir，我从你所说的话中了解到，人们对这些摄像头感到不满，并且有许多不同的隐私担忧。

sentences.en: But I wonder how much of these concerns are theoretical at this point?
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，这些担忧在目前看来有多少是理论上的？

sentences.en: Or are critics saying that there's already evidence that these cameras have been misused?
sentences.zh: 还是说批评者认为已经有证据表明这些摄像头被滥用了？

sentences.en: Yeah, one of the cases that has gotten the most attention and was originally reported by 404 Media was a woman who was suspected of self-administering an abortion in Texas.
sentences.zh: 是的，其中一个引起最多关注且最初由404 Media报道的案例，是一名在德克萨斯州涉嫌自行堕胎的女性。

sentences.en: And an officer searched flock cameras to see where she had traveled if she was out of state to try to track her down.
sentences.zh: 一名警官搜索了Flock摄像头，查看她是否去了州外，试图追踪她。

sentences.en: There have been examples of police officers abusing their access to these systems to track exes or love interests or romantic partners.
sentences.zh: 已经有警察滥用他们对这些系统的访问权限来追踪前任、恋人或浪漫伴侣的例子。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And one of the kind of big concerns has been how immigration officers are using these cameras for immigration enforcement.
sentences.zh: 其中一个很大的担忧是移民官员如何利用这些摄像头进行移民执法。

sentences.en: You mean like ICE, like trying to track down people they're trying to deport?
sentences.zh: 你是说像ICE（美国移民及海关执法局）那样，试图追踪他们想要驱逐出境的人？

sentences.en: Yes, ICE trying to track down people that they want to deport.
sentences.zh: 是的，ICE试图追踪他们想要驱逐出境的人。

sentences.en: And it's not just civil libertarians that are criticizing this.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是公民自由主义者在批评这一点。

sentences.en: Cities themselves have been surprised that their cameras have been accessed for immigration enforcement.
sentences.zh: 城市本身也对他们的摄像头被用于移民执法感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So some cities have paused or canceled their contracts with Flock after discovering that because they basically didn't realize that when they were making it available nationally,
sentences.zh: 因此，一些城市在发现这一点后暂停或取消了与Flock的合同，因为他们基本上没有意识到，当他们将其提供给全国使用时，

sentences.en: that meant they're making it available to federal law enforcement like ICE.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们将其提供给了像ICE这样的联邦执法机构。

sentences.en: That feels a little bit surprising, though, Kashmir, because you said earlier that they signed something saying, like, their databases are searchable.
sentences.zh: Kashmir，这听起来有点令人惊讶，因为你之前说过他们签署了协议，说他们的数据库是可以搜索的。

sentences.en: So were you surprised that they were surprised?
sentences.zh: 所以你对他们感到惊讶这件事感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: That just feels a little bit strange.
sentences.zh: 这感觉有点奇怪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, Flock says that they don't have a contract with ICE, for one.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，Flock说他们并没有与ICE签订合同。

sentences.en: And the way that this is happening is actually ICE agents are partnering with local police departments and then searching the networks of cameras that they have access to.
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生的方式实际上是ICE特工与当地警察部门合作，然后搜索他们有权访问的摄像头网络。

sentences.en: So it's not necessarily the police department that they're partnering with that is upset over this.
sentences.zh: 所以不一定是对这个感到不满的警察部门与他们合作。

sentences.en: It's the police department in another city that is learning that ICE is using them.
sentences.zh: 而是另一个城市的警察部门得知ICE正在使用他们的摄像头。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is kind of a concept called networked privacy, where it's hard to protect your own privacy.
sentences.zh: 这是一种被称为“网络隐私”的概念，保护自己的隐私变得很难。

sentences.en: Since they're sharing it with others, they have to trust that other agencies are using the cameras appropriately.
sentences.zh: 由于他们与他人共享，他们必须信任其他机构正在适当地使用这些摄像头。

sentences.en: And this actually comes up on the sign-in page.
sentences.zh: 这实际上出现在登录页面上。

sentences.en: There's kind of this pop-up.
sentences.zh: 有一种弹出窗口。

sentences.en: There's a click-through screen where you have to say, I acknowledge that in these states, I can't do searches related to reproductive care.
sentences.zh: 有一个点击通过的屏幕，你必须确认：我承认在这些州，我不能进行与生殖保健相关的搜索。

sentences.en: And in these other states, I can't do searches related to immigration.
sentences.zh: 而在其他州，我不能进行与移民相关的搜索。

sentences.en: So it sounds like a little bit of an honor system.
sentences.zh: 所以这听起来有点像是一种荣誉制度。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm curious what else the company has told you about the safeguards it has in place to prevent misuse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我很好奇该公司还告诉了你什么关于它为防止滥用而采取的保障措施。

sentences.en: Because, I don't know, I just can't imagine how effective that actually is if you're a bad actor, you know, operating in bad faith.
sentences.zh: 因为，我不知道，我无法想象如果你是一个恶意行为者，你知道，心怀不轨，这到底有多有效。

sentences.en: Flock says that they only allow abortion-related searches in states where abortion is illegal.
sentences.zh: Flock表示，他们只允许在堕胎非法的州进行与堕胎相关的搜索。

sentences.en: They also say that they have an audit system in place that alerts departments if officers are doing unusual searching.
sentences.zh: 他们还表示，他们有一个审计系统，如果警官进行异常搜索，会向部门发出警报。

sentences.en: That doesn't look like it's related to an official investigation.
sentences.zh: 这看起来与官方调查无关。

sentences.en: So they do say they have some safeguards in place.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实说他们采取了一些保障措施。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, it's up to the police departments to use this tool appropriately.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这取决于警察部门是否适当地使用这个工具。

sentences.en: Flock doesn't consider itself the one that should make the rules for how these cameras should work.
sentences.zh: Flock并不认为自己应该是制定这些摄像头如何工作规则的人。

sentences.en: It says, you know, it's just a technology company offering a service.
sentences.zh: 它说，你知道，它只是一家提供服务的技术公司。

sentences.en: And it's up to the United States to decide how these cameras should be used.
sentences.zh: 如何使用这些摄像头取决于美国政府。

sentences.en: Why should we put restraints on our own growth when there's no law preventing us from growing as fast as we can?
sentences.zh: 当没有任何法律阻止我们尽可能快地增长时，我们为什么要限制自己的增长？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're just a company offering a service.
sentences.zh: 他们只是一家提供服务的公司。

sentences.en: And it's not up to them to make the rules.
sentences.zh: 制定规则不是他们的事。

sentences.en: That's up to lawmakers.
sentences.zh: 那是立法者的事。

sentences.en: That's up to regulators.
sentences.zh: 那是监管机构的事。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm really starting to get a sense, Kashmir, from the picture that you're painting of why people are maybe upset.
sentences.zh: 好的，Kashmir，从你描绘的图景中，我真的开始明白为什么人们可能会感到不安了。

sentences.en: I mean, this company really does not seem to be doing a ton to block bad actors from abusing its platforMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这家公司似乎确实没有做太多工作来阻止恶意行为者滥用其平台。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure that it would say that it is and it has pop-ups.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我相信它会说它做了，而且它有弹出窗口。

sentences.en: But as you described, this is an honor system with no government intervention or regulation.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所描述的，这是一个没有政府干预或监管的荣誉制度。

sentences.en: It seems like the government has not caught up to this technology.
sentences.zh: 看起来政府还没有跟上这项技术的发展。

sentences.en: And that sounds like something that would be concerning for people.
sentences.zh: 这听起来确实是人们会担心的事情。

sentences.en: Yes, there is this growing backlash from citizens.
sentences.zh: 是的，公民中确实存在这种日益增长的抵制情绪。

sentences.en: One of the first ways this manifested was in the form of a website called Deflock.
sentences.zh: 这种情绪最初的表现形式之一是一个名为Deflock的网站。

sentences.en: Deflock, like D-E-Flock.
sentences.zh: Deflock，就像D-E-Flock。

sentences.en: It's a crowdsource map of where these cameras, these license plate readers are that anyone can contribute to.
sentences.zh: 这是一个众包地图，标明了这些摄像头、这些车牌阅读器的位置，任何人都可以贡献信息。

sentences.en: And the idea is that you should know how many are in your community and where they are.
sentences.zh: 其理念是，你应该知道你的社区里有多少个摄像头，以及它们在哪里。

sentences.en: And now they've mapped over 100,000 cameras made by Flock and other companies.
sentences.zh: 现在他们已经绘制了超过10万个由Flock和其他公司制造的摄像头。

sentences.en: And you started seeing some people cutting down cameras.
sentences.zh: 而且你开始看到有些人开始拆除摄像头了。

sentences.en: A vandal cut down a Flock pole, spray painted the lens black, and cut the wiring.
sentences.zh: 有破坏者砍倒了一根Flock监控杆，用喷漆把摄像头涂黑，还剪断了电线。

sentences.en: Like spray painting them, vandalizing them.
sentences.zh: 比如喷漆涂抹，对它们进行破坏。

sentences.en: Several cameras were ripped from their mouths and smashed.
sentences.zh: 好几台摄像头被从安装座上硬生生扯下来砸碎了。

sentences.en: Allegedly using a shotgun to take out Flock cameras.
sentences.zh: 据称有人用霰弹枪去打掉Flock摄像头。

sentences.en: Both cameras were later found in a nearby canal.
sentences.zh: 两台摄像头后来在附近的运河里被发现。

sentences.en: There have been videos of people demonstrating how to like get rid of the cameras, how to destroy them.
sentences.zh: 网上有一些视频，演示人们如何摆脱这些摄像头，如何摧毁它们。

sentences.en: With their saw wrapped in a trash bag, they approach from behind the camera's line of sight and tear right through this black aluminum alloy poSt.
sentences.zh: 他们用垃圾袋包住锯子，从摄像头的盲区绕到后面，直接锯断了这根黑色铝合金杆。

sentences.en: People have showed up at city council hearings.
sentences.zh: 人们出现在市议会的听证会上。

sentences.en: In free America, where I go during the day, is my business.
sentences.zh: 在自由的美国，我白天去哪儿是我的私事。

sentences.en: Saying, I am not happy about this.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我对这个很不满。

sentences.en: We want everything out of our city, get out of our police state.
sentences.zh: 我们想把所有这些东西赶出我们的城市，滚出我们的警察国家。

sentences.en: We're being tracked everywhere we go.
sentences.zh: 我们无论走到哪里都被追踪。

sentences.en: And y'all are just saying, you're being tracked anyway.
sentences.zh: 而你们只是说，反正你们也一直被追踪着。

sentences.en: There was another super viral video of this one guy in San Diego who went to the city council hearing, dressed up as Darth Vader.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个超级火的视频，圣地亚哥有个家伙打扮成达斯·维达去参加市议会听证会。

sentences.en: The emperor is a fan of Flock.
sentences.zh: 皇帝是Flock的粉丝。

sentences.en: Saying how much he loved Flock cameras.
sentences.zh: 他说他有多么喜欢Flock摄像头。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And we must continue utilizing Flock technologies so that we can follow and surveil the rebel scum.
sentences.zh: 我们必须继续利用Flock技术，这样我们才能追踪和监视那些反叛的人渣。

sentences.en: Some citizens have sued their cities or their towns saying that these cameras are unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 一些市民起诉了他们所在的城市或城镇，称这些摄像头违宪。

sentences.en: Oh wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: They're unconstitutional because they are capturing everyone's movements.
sentences.zh: 它们违宪，因为它们在捕捉每个人的行踪。

sentences.en: Even if you've done nothing wrong, for most places it's capturing the last 30 days of people driving around on the roads.
sentences.zh: 即使你没做错任何事，在大多数地方，它都在记录人们过去30天在路上的驾驶轨迹。

sentences.en: And that this is something that the Fourth Amendment is supposed to protect us againSt.
sentences.zh: 而这正是宪法第四修正案理应保护我们免受侵害的对象。

sentences.en: The Fourth Amendment, that is the amendment that prohibits unlawful searches and seizures.
sentences.zh: 第四修正案，就是禁止非法搜查和扣押的那条修正案。

sentences.en: Just explain one beat farther, Cash, why that is relevant to these cameras, this network, this idea of capturing people who haven't done anything wrong.
sentences.zh: Cash，再多解释一点，为什么这与这些摄像头、这个网络，以及捕捉那些没做错事的人的想法有关？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean the idea behind the Fourth Amendment, if we go back to the Founding Fathers,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，如果我们回顾开国元勋们制定第四修正案时的初衷，

sentences.en: is that they didn't like that, you know, royal officers would just go through everybody's houses,
sentences.zh: 是因为他们不喜欢那种皇家官员随意搜查每个人家里的做法，

sentences.en: rifle through their drawers, looking for evidence that they were involved in treason or rebellion.
sentences.zh: 翻箱倒柜，寻找他们参与叛国或叛乱的证据。

sentences.en: The Fourth Amendment was created so that police have to have a reason to think that someone has done something wrong before they collect information about them.
sentences.zh: 第四修正案的设立，是为了让警察在收集某人的信息之前，必须有理由认为此人做了错事。

sentences.en: But that's not what these cameras are.
sentences.zh: 但这些摄像头不是这样。

sentences.en: They're everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它们无处不在。

sentences.en: They're collecting data on hundreds of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 它们正在收集数亿人的数据。

sentences.en: They get billions of license plate reads.
sentences.zh: 它们每天获得数十亿次车牌识别记录。

sentences.en: And so some of these lawsuits have said, you can't do this.
sentences.zh: 所以一些诉讼指出，你们不能这样做。

sentences.en: And so far, those lawsuits have not been successful.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，这些诉讼都没有成功。

sentences.en: But in some of the rulings, the judges have said, well, if these cameras were more ubiquitous, then yes, there would be Fourth Amendment concerns.
sentences.zh: 但在一些裁决中，法官们表示，如果这些摄像头更加普及，那么是的，确实会引发第四修正案的担忧。

sentences.en: Basically, they're not widespread enough yet.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它们还不够普及。

sentences.en: Wait, that's so interesting, though.
sentences.zh: 等等，这太有意思了。

sentences.en: Like, who gets to decide what the threshold is for ubiquity for these cameras?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁来决定这些摄像头普及程度的门槛是什么？

sentences.en: Like, who gets to decide, OK, this is the level of penetration that would be violative of the Fourth Amendment?
sentences.zh: 谁来决定，好吧，达到这种渗透程度就会违反第四修正案？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, judges decide.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，由法官来决定。

sentences.en: Maybe one day the Supreme Court will decide.
sentences.zh: 也许有一天最高法院会做出裁决。

sentences.en: When I talk to attorneys in the civil liberty space, they say, we're already there.
sentences.zh: 当我与民权领域的律师交谈时，他们说，我们已经达到那个程度了。

sentences.en: Judges just don't understand how many of these cameras there are and how networked they are.
sentences.zh: 只是法官们不了解这些摄像头到底有多少，以及它们的网络化程度有多高。

sentences.en: I'm just so curious what evidence the judges are looking at to say, no, this is not actually broad enough.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇法官们在看什么证据，从而得出结论说，不，这实际上还不够广泛。

sentences.en: As you said, 40 percent of police departments are using this, billions of hits a day.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，40%的警察局都在使用它，每天有数十亿次命中记录。

sentences.en: What is the standard that they're using?
sentences.zh: 他们使用的标准到底是什么？

sentences.en: So, in Norfolk, Virginia, where one of these lawsuits was filed, the city now has 172 flat cameras installed around the city.
sentences.zh: 在弗吉尼亚州的诺福克，其中一起诉讼就是在那里提起的，该市现在安装了172台Flock摄像头。

sentences.en: And the judge said, that's not enough.
sentences.zh: 法官说，这还不够多。

sentences.en: But the judge didn't say, what is the number where it's too much?
sentences.zh: 但法官并没有说，到底多少才算太多？

sentences.en: Is it, you know, every block?
sentences.zh: 是每个街区都要有吗？

sentences.en: Is it every street?
sentences.zh: 是每条街道都要有吗？

sentences.en: What level of coverage hits that threshold?
sentences.zh: 什么样的覆盖水平才达到那个门槛？

sentences.en: That hasn't been spelled out yet.
sentences.zh: 这一点还没有明确说明。

sentences.en: It sounds a little arbitrary at this point.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，听起来有点武断。

sentences.en: Welcome to the law, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到法律的世界，Rachel。

sentences.en: Especially around privacy.
sentences.zh: 特别是在隐私方面。

sentences.en: I mean, privacy is so hard to define, you know, what is an unreasonable search.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，隐私太难定义了，你知道，什么是不合理的搜查。

sentences.en: That is something that is always getting worked out.
sentences.zh: 这是一个一直在不断完善的问题。

sentences.en: But what the court has found in the past is that, you know, police can't just put a tracker on someone's car, for example.
sentences.zh: 但法院过去发现的是，警察不能随意在某人的车上安装追踪器，例如。

sentences.en: Even though they're on public roads and a police officer could follow them, that this idea of using automated means to track somebody continually violates Fourth Amendment.
sentences.zh: 尽管车在公共道路上行驶，警察也可以跟踪，但这种使用自动化手段持续追踪某人的做法违反了第四修正案。

sentences.en: And what lawyers I talk to argue is, well, we're doing the same thing now, but instead of putting trackers on people's cars,
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的律师们认为，好吧，我们现在做的是同样的事情，但不是在人们的车上安装追踪器，

sentences.en: we're just putting these cameras everywhere on the roads.
sentences.zh: 我们只是把这些摄像头安装在道路上的各个地方。

sentences.en: We have talked a lot in this conversation about people who are worried about privacy.
sentences.zh: 在这次谈话中，我们谈了很多关于担心隐私的人。

sentences.en: But there are also a lot of people in this country who are really worried about crime.
sentences.zh: 但这个国家也有很多人非常担心犯罪问题。

sentences.en: Like, I don't even know, to the extent that these two groups of people are distinct, which one of them is bigger.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道，这两类人有多大程度上的重叠，哪一类人更多。

sentences.en: So I wonder how we're supposed to think about Flock when we hold up these two kind of competing concerns against one another, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，当我们把这两种相互竞争的担忧放在一起衡量时，我们该如何看待Flock？

sentences.en: People who are really worried, maybe more so about getting their license plate readers read versus people who are like, I don't want crime in my communities.
sentences.zh: 是那些更担心车牌被读取的人，还是那些说我不想让社区里有犯罪的人？

sentences.en: I'm more worried about crime than I am of somebody taking a picture of my car.
sentences.zh: 我更担心犯罪，而不是有人拍了我的车。

sentences.en: I mean, that is the legal question here and kind of the societal question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是这里的法律问题，也是某种社会问题。

sentences.en: What degree of liberty do we want to give up for security?
sentences.zh: 为了安全，我们愿意放弃多少自由？

sentences.en: We'll never have perfect liberty.
sentences.zh: 我们永远不会拥有完美的自由。

sentences.en: We'll never have perfect security.
sentences.zh: 我们永远不会拥有完美的安全。

sentences.en: What struck me about the reaction to Flock Cameras is just how bipartisan it is.
sentences.zh: Flock摄像头的反应让我震惊的是，它是多么的两党一致。

sentences.en: People on the left and the right have objections to these cameras.
sentences.zh: 左派和右派的人都对这些摄像头有异议。

sentences.en: It's kind of across the board.
sentences.zh: 这在各个层面都是如此。

sentences.en: And so that's been really striking.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点真的很引人注目。

sentences.en: One of the experts I talked to said there is a version of this where we could just have the cameras give alerts and not be tracking us for seven days or 30 days or five years in the case of some states.
sentences.zh: 我采访的一位专家说，有一种方案是，我们可以只让摄像头发出警报，而不是追踪我们七天、30天，甚至在某些州长达五年。

sentences.en: Let's say you have to retain, you know, the photos of these cars for that long.
sentences.zh: 假设你必须保留这些车辆的照片那么久。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a question of every surveillance technology, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是所有监控技术的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: If you had perfect surveillance, we could live in a country with very little crime, but it would certainly violate some of our constitutional principles.
sentences.zh: 如果你有完美的监控，我们可以生活在一个几乎没有犯罪的国家，但这肯定会违反我们的一些宪法原则。

sentences.en: I feel like most of my adult life, which has existed mostly in the post-Edward Snowden era, people have been talking about privacy and surveillance.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我成年后的大部分时间，基本是在爱德华·斯诺登时代之后度过的，人们一直在谈论隐私和监控。

sentences.en: And for all of those concerns, though, technology just marches on.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管有这些担忧，技术还是在不断进步。

sentences.en: Like, it feels like even though we might be worried about this kind of stuff, we've given up a lot of privacy in exchange for convenience.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像，即使我们可能担心这类事情，我们也为了便利而放弃了很多隐私。

sentences.en: Like, that does feel like the world we are living in.
sentences.zh: 这确实感觉像是我们所处的世界。

sentences.en: But I do feel like this issue with Flock, it feels like it is hitting a different kind of nerve.
sentences.zh: 但我确实觉得Flock这个问题，触动了某种不同的神经。

sentences.en: And part of me wonders why that is.
sentences.zh: 我的一部分在想为什么会这样。

sentences.en: Like, is it because of the physicality of being able to see a camera, knowing that it is tracking my car, my person, I guess?
sentences.zh: 是因为能看到摄像头的物理存在感吗？知道它在追踪我的车，或者说我的个人行踪？

sentences.en: Like, the fact that you can go out and break one.
sentences.zh: 比如，你可以走出去砸烂一个。

sentences.en: How much of that crash do you think is part of why we're seeing so much anger about this system?
sentences.zh: 你认为这种破坏行为在多大程度上导致了我们对这个系统如此愤怒？

sentences.en: I think the physicality does play a role here.
sentences.zh: 我认为物理存在感确实在其中发挥了作用。

sentences.en: You know, so many of our privacy concerns are around invisible tracking and data collection that happens online.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们太多的隐私担忧是关于在线发生的隐形追踪和数据收集。

sentences.en: And this time you can actually see it and how and where it's happening.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，你可以亲眼看到它，看到它是如何以及在哪里发生的。

sentences.en: But I also think there are bigger issues at play here.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这里还有更大的问题。

sentences.en: Part of it is that private companies have stepped in to do surveillance that previously the government would have been forbidden from doing.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是私营公司介入了政府以前被禁止进行的监控活动。

sentences.en: And I saw this before covering Clearview AI, this company that scraped everybody's photos to build a facial recognition app that police could use to identify people.
sentences.zh: 我在报道Clearview AI之前就看到了这一点，这家公司抓取了所有人的照片来构建一个面部识别应用程序，警察可以用它来识别身份。

sentences.en: It's the same thing with Flock.
sentences.zh: Flock也是一样。

sentences.en: You know, they've created this huge database and then they sell it to law enforcement so they can just use it without getting a warrant.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们建立了一个庞大的数据库，然后把它卖给执法部门，这样他们就可以在没有搜查令的情况下直接使用它。

sentences.en: And it's also just this growing amount of technology.
sentences.zh: 而且这仅仅是不断增长的技术总量的一部分。

sentences.en: There's so many new ways to track us, to observe us, to create these running databases that are so huge.
sentences.zh: 有太多新的方法来追踪我们、观察我们、创建这些如此庞大的运行数据库。

sentences.en: And I think this one kind of very slowly crept up on us.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个系统是慢慢地向我们逼近的。

sentences.en: It was like people weren't paying enough attention to Flock.
sentences.zh: 就像人们对Flock的关注还不够。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden we realized there's 120,000 cameras across the country.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，我们意识到全国有12万台摄像头。

sentences.en: And as one source put it to me, we're just sleepwalking into this surveillance state where it's just too easy to know everything about us.
sentences.zh: 正如一位消息人士对我所说，我们正在梦游般地进入这个监控国家，在这里，了解关于我们的一切变得太容易了。

sentences.en: Kashmir Hill, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: Kashmir Hill，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 周日对伊朗进行了自一个月以来的首次打击。

sentences.zh: 据美国。

sentences.zh: 中央司令部称，美军袭击了霍尔木兹海峡一个岛屿上的两个伊朗火箭发射器。

sentences.zh: 这似乎是一次有限的打击，而不是大规模轰炸。

sentences.zh: 但伊朗表示将进行报复，这增加了持续军事打击的风险。
